compensating.why: hop 4 copies the field at which the parser stands before handing the parser to the gold
hop 1 writes the START_OBJECT that the parser has already read before passing the parser on
hop 4 accepts whatever token ended the copy

expected_signature: Expected END_OBJECT after copying contents of a JsonParser into TokenBuffer, got VALUE_NUMBER_INT
ownership_reason: Only the gold reads the fields of the Object and decides where the copy starts: it writes START_OBJECT itself, then must copy the field at which the parser already stands before advancing with nextToken(); hops 2-3 pass the buffer, the parser and the context along unchanged, hop 1 only copies a parser that is not at a field name whole, and hop 4 only checks that the token the gold returns is END_OBJECT. The gold's javadoc promises the fields of the JSON Object the parser is reading, copied as one complete Object, which the variant does not deliver for a parser at the first field name (that field is skipped). No one-line change above the gold restores the stream: a caller cannot rewind the parser, copying the current field above the gold puts it before the START_OBJECT the gold writes, writing START_OBJECT above the gold gives two, and dropping hop 4's check returns an empty Object. The convention that a parser at FIELD_NAME is already inside the Object and that its CURRENT field is the first one is pinned by production deserializers: UntypedObjectDeserializer.mapObject (key1 = p.getCurrentName() at FIELD_NAME), MapDeserializer._readAndBindStringMap and _readAndBind (keyStr = p.getCurrentName() when not at START_OBJECT), with TestCreators2 testIssue465 and testAbstractFactory (a delegating Map creator, which receives a parser at the first field name, keeps the first entry); hop 1's javadoc states it for this chain.
